subject: MedLytics: confirmation of prompt/output handling, retention, and US-only residency
messages:

Subject: Discovery recap: prompt auditing, retention, and geographic controls (MedLytics)

Hi Katie / Legal team 3 thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we agreed to follow up on: 

Summary: MedLytics will use our API for a symptom-triage assistant; some prompts contain patient identifiers (PHI). Key areas: what we store, how long, and whether storage can be limited to US regions only.

MedLytics asks (we captured):
1) Which artifacts are written to persistent logs (prompts, completions, user identifiers, IPs, timestamps, traces).
2) Default retention and minimum configurable retention windows for each artifact.
3) Whether a zero-retention / ephemeral mode is available for hosted API and what feature tradeoffs that causes.
4) KV cache persistence behavior.
5) KMS / key options for Dedicated and Private, and single-region residency guarantees for logs/backups.

Action items:
- Vanessa: consolidate definitive answers with engineering & compliance and send by Tue 2026-04-21 EOD.
- Karthik / Markus: please flag any constraints on zero-retention and KV cache.

Attachments: redwood-data-practices.pdf (summary), retention-config.yml (example config), procurement-statement-draft.docx (blank draft for Legal).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Katie Holmes <katie.holmes@medlytics.com>

Date: 2026-04-18T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: prompt auditing, retention, and geographic controls (MedLytics)

Thanks Vanessa 3 useful recap. A couple quick clarifications for our security team: 

- A) Do hosted API calls write raw prompt text to any long-term analytics, observability, or audit stores by default? If yes, what is the default retention?
- B) Are model outputs (completions) treated the same as prompts in retention and logs?
- C) Can we opt into a hosted "ephemeral mode" where neither prompts nor completions are persisted beyond in-memory processing? Any feature limitations (e.g., no streaming, no diagnostics)?
- D) Does KV cache ever touch disk or persistent storage, or is it strictly in-memory and ephemeral per-host?
- E) For Dedicated/Private: is customer-managed KMS supported and can backups/logs be kept within the customer's VPC / US-only region?

Legal wants a short, copy-pasteable statement they can drop into procurement that says exactly what will and will not be stored and the retention/region commitments.

-Katie
Katie Holmes
Head of Product Partnerships, MedLytics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Holmes <katie.holmes@medlytics.com>, MedLytics Legal <legal@medlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-21T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MedLytics: confirmation of prompt/output handling, retention, and US-only residency

Hi Katie / Legal 3 appreciate the patience while we pulled in engineering and compliance. Below wedve provided definitive answers for Hosted API and notes for Dedicated/Private. Idve also attached a short one-paragraph procurement statement (procurement-statement-draft.docx) you can drop in a PO.

Short answers (Hosted API):
- Persisted artifacts: by default Redwood Analytics writes request metadata (timestamp, model id, request size, latency, anonymized route id) to our analytics cluster. Raw prompt text and model completions are not written to long-term analytics by default unless the customer explicitly enables logging (see opt-in below).
- Default retention: analytics metadata default 90 days; configurable down to 0 days for analytics only.
- Raw prompts & completions: hosted customers can enable full request/response logging for debugging; when enabled, those artifacts are stored in a configurable log stream. If you do not enable logging, prompts and completions are ephemeral and not persisted to long-term stores.
- Ephemeral/zero-retention mode: we support an opt-in "no-persist" mode for hosted customers where prompts and completions are not written to any persistent stores and diagnostics are limited (no streaming logs, no retained traces). This mode is available but disables some debugging features and may limit performance telemetry.
- KV cache: inference KV cache is in-memory on the serving host and is not persisted to disk in our standard runtime. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers can configure persistent cache; default Dedicated deployment keeps cache in-memory unless configured otherwise.

Dedicated / Private notes:
- KMS / BYOK: customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated and Private (BYOK through supported cloud KMS providers or HSM for on-prem).
- Residency: Dedicated and Private can be configured to keep logs/backups inside a single customer-selected US region and within the customer's VPC for Private deployments. Hosted API customers may be restricted to region selections offered in our hosted catalog; we can commit to US-only hosted regions for contractual agreements (single-region lock) if requested in the SOW.
- Deletion & certification: deletion requests are supported. For hosted analytics we can scrub logs and issue a deletion confirmation. For Dedicated/Private we provide tooling and playbooks for deletion and can include certification language in an addendum. Backups: destruction is handled per our backup lifecycle; we can include contractual guarantees for backup overwrite timing where required.

Procurement-ready paragraph (drop-in):
"Redwood Inference confirms that, by default, hosted API customers do not have raw prompt text or model completions persisted to Redwood's long-term analytics stores unless explicit logging is enabled. Analytics metadata (timestamps, model id, latency, anonymized route identifiers) are retained by default for 90 days and may be configured to a minimum of 0 days. Redwood supports a hosted "no-persist" mode that prevents prompts and completions from being written to persistent storage (feature tradeoffs apply). For Dedicated and Private deployments, Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) and can guarantee that logs and backups remain within a single US region or inside the customer's VPC; deletion and backup overwrite procedures can be provided and certified under a contract addendum where required."

Next steps:
- If Legal is happy with the paragraph above we can include it in the SOW. If you require additional binding language (e.g., SLA for deletion timing), we will route to Legal for an addendum.
- Karthik / Markus: please review and flag any technical inaccuracies.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
